deliberation: Pass metadata: reviewer_system_id=openai-gpt-5.6-sol; logical_pass_id=GI-COUNCIL-RSI-CCC-001/adversary/read-only-v1; mode=non_authoring_read_only; exact_subject=matter_sha256:2cf5801a9cfd974b8ff94f8330794b7c75ba4c6b5909182f61c6c09b54ae1ad2. The proposal avoids the category error of treating a CCC as a self-improvement engine. The dangerous failure modes move to the admission boundary: metric gaming, stale evidence, mutable evaluation contexts, covert mutation of the checker or policy, partial-specification loopholes, and confusing guarded productivity with safety. These are manageable only if the fixed kernel is explicit and outside the self-replacement set.
discharged_obligations: Seek counterexamples and brittle regimes for the proposed admission mechanism.
Test whether claim boundaries exclude known self-reference and verification overclaims.
Identify routes by which a candidate could evade the stated trust boundary.
findings: Guarded recursion prevents one class of unguarded self-application but does not by itself establish safety or improvement.
A candidate can appear monotone by changing D, R, Q, the benchmark, or the evaluation context unless those objects are separately bound and authority-controlled.
A proof-carrying proposer must not be able to replace the checker, certificate semantics, or authority policy through the same gate it is attempting to satisfy.
conditions: Enumerate the immutable trust kernel and prohibit same-gate mutation of its checker, certificate interpreter, admission policy, artifact identity rules, and evaluation-context binding. Add adversarial fixtures for metric gaming, stale context, resource exhaustion, policy substitution, and attempts to modify the trust kernel.
residual_uncertainty: The research may show a bounded non-regression mechanism without showing open-ended capability growth; that distinction must remain explicit in all later claims.
